title: What does the zero do in four thousand seventy two?
description: The number four thousand seventy two is read as digits times powers of ten, and the job of its zero is explained. Keeko's doubt is that the zero can be left out because it is worth nothing.
teaching_notes: One idea: a zero is worth nothing itself but holds an empty place so the other digits keep their values. Watch for students who drop the zero and let the other digits slide into the wrong places.

source: Read 4072 as digits times powers of 10, and explain what the 0 does.
video_script.why: The child writes a four digit number as digits times powers of ten and sees that the zero holds the empty hundreds place.
video_script.substitution: Name the places, write each digit times the power of ten of its place, and check by adding the values.
video_script.anchor: the book's Hindu number system: digits from 0 to 9 in places, each worth ten times the place on its right
video_script.wrong_answer: leave out the zero and write four seven two
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko drops the 0 because it is worth nothing, so 4, 7, 2 reads 472, not 4072; the digits slide into the wrong places
video_script.payoff_line: The zero holds the empty hundreds place, so four, zero, seven, two make four thousand seventy two.

final_answer.value: 4072 = (4) × 10³ + (0) × 10² + (7) × 10 + (2) × 1; the 0 holds the empty hundreds place
final_answer.spoken: four thousand seventy two is four times ten cubed, plus zero times ten squared, plus seven times ten, plus two times one; the zero holds the empty hundreds place

hold_back: 4072 = (4) × 10³ + (0) × 10² + (7) × 10 + (2) × 1; the 0 holds the empty hundreds place
maths_rules: 4072: 2 in the 1s place, 7 in the 10s place, 0 in the 100s place, 4 in the 1000s place
the 0 says there are no hundreds and keeps the 4 and the 7 in their places
Keeko's slip: leaving out the 0 makes 4, 7, 2 read 472

narration: <bookmark mark='ten'/>The Hindu number system is a base ten system. Each place is worth ten times the place on its right.
<bookmark mark='digits'/>Every place holds one digit, from zero to nine.
<bookmark mark='zero'/>The digit zero stands in a place where there is nothing to count.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the number four thousand seventy two.

narration: <bookmark mark='places'/>Step one, name the places from the right. They are ones, tens, hundreds and thousands.
<bookmark mark='digits'/>The two is in the ones place and the seven is in the tens place. <bookmark mark='hund'/>The zero is in the hundreds place, and the four is in the thousands place.
<bookmark mark='big'/>Step two, write each digit times the power of ten of its place. That is four times ten cubed, plus zero times ten squared.
<bookmark mark='small'/>Then come seven times ten, and two times one.
<bookmark mark='check'/>Step three, check by adding the values. Four thousand plus nothing plus seventy plus two gives the number we began with.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko wants to leave out the zero and write four seven two, because zero is worth nothing.
<bookmark mark='slide'/>Then the digits would slide over, and the number would read four hundred seventy two.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The zero is worth nothing, but its place is not. It keeps the four in the thousands place.
